# TabScaffold

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:tab-scaffold` · Kerf UI · component · Structure

A controlled compact-device bottom tab scaffold that keeps every tab scene mounted so its navigation and scroll state survive selection changes.

## When to use

Switch among two to five co-equal top-level destinations on compact devices while preserving each destination's independent content state.

- A handset or portrait-tablet app has two to five co-equal top-level destinations.
- Each destination must stay mounted so its NavStack and scroll position survive tab switches.

**Not when:**

- Do not use TabScaffold for document tabs or reorderable work items; use TabBar.
- Do not retain the bottom bar on desktop when the same destinations should be promoted to a Workbench rail or sidebar.

**Alternatives:**

- [AppTab](./tabs.md) (semantic-alternative) — Use TabBar and AppTab for document-style tabpanels, overflow, closing, or reordering.
- [Workbench](./workbench.md) (roomy-alternative) — Promote top-level destinations to a rail or sidebar on desktop-class layouts.

## Imports

- JavaScript: `@kerfjs/ui/tab-scaffold` — exports `TabScaffoldTab`, `TabScaffoldProps`, `TabScaffold`.
- CSS: import `@kerfjs/ui/tab-scaffold.css` once.
- Wiring: `wireTabScaffold` from `@kerfjs/ui/wire-tab-scaffold` (required).
- Declared side effects: manual-css.

## Props

Exact prop names and types: [`@kerfjs/ui/tab-scaffold`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuitab-scaffold), [`@kerfjs/ui/wire-tab-scaffold`](../public-api-signatures-v1.md#kerfjsuiwire-tab-scaffold) in `public-api-signatures-v1.md`. Do not infer props from examples.

**Variants (configure, do not restyle):**

- text-only tabs
- icon and text tabs
- badged tabs (count or text-free dot)
- one NavStack per tab

## Composition

- Parents: any.
- Contexts: `application-ui`.
- Children: unrestricted.
- Built from: [Badge](./badge.md).

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** controlled active tab id; tab labels, icons, and content; tab badge counts or dots and their localized badgeLabel phrases; routing and persistence; responsive replacement on larger device classes.

**Wiring:** `wireTabScaffold` is required.

- Use wireTabScaffold as documented.

## Geometry

Margin: none · border: self · padding: self (layout role: structure). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

- The scaffold owns the full-height scene region and safe-area-aware bottom bar; scene content owns its internal geometry.

## Accessibility

- Give the tablist an accessible label and keep exactly the active tab in the sequential focus order.
- Wire selection through the controlled active id while leaving inactive scenes mounted and hidden.
- A tab badge is aria-hidden; supply badgeLabel so the tab's accessible name becomes "\<label>, \<badgeLabel>" (it defaults to the badge text). The dot form, badge: true, has no text, so its badgeLabel is required.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Public class hooks (select for layout placement only, never to change the component's look): `kui-tab-scaffold`, `kui-tab-scaffold__scenes`, `kui-tab-scaffold__scene`, `kui-tab-scaffold__bar`, `kui-tab-scaffold__tab`, `kui-tab-scaffold__tab-icon`, `kui-tab-scaffold__tab-badge`, `kui-tab-scaffold__tab-label`.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and forced component dimensions (`KUI-L005`).
